claims.text: The investigated alloy has an approximate composition of Ti40Ni40Cr10Al5V5.
The solution-treated Ti40Ni40Cr10Al5V5 alloy is a single-phase BCC disordered solid solution.
Solution treatment at approximately 1050 °C homogenizes the alloy.
Aging the solutionized alloy at 700 °C for 1–3 hours under inert atmosphere promotes TiNi intermetallic precipitation.
The proposed aging treatment can produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale TiNi precipitates.
The TiNi precipitates formed by aging will be coherent with the high-entropy-alloy matrix.
TiNi precipitates impede dislocation movement at elevated temperatures.
TiNi precipitates impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperatures.
Obstruction of dislocation movement by TiNi precipitates increases elevated-temperature yield strength through precipitation strengthening.
Obstruction of grain-boundary sliding by TiNi precipitates improves creep resistance.
The aged alloy will have more than approximately 20–30% greater elevated-temperature yield strength than the as-solutionized alloy.
The aged alloy will have better elevated-temperature creep resistance than the as-solutionized alloy.
The aged alloy will retain adequate ductility if its precipitates remain nanoscale and well dispersed.
Excessive aging can coarsen the precipitates.
Deviation from the optimal aging temperature can cause undesired phase transformations.
Precipitate coarsening or undesired phase transformations compromise the alloy's mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The proposed Ti40Ni40Cr10Al5V5 composition assigns 40 at% each to Ti and Ni, exceeding the stated high-entropy-alloy boundary of 5–35 at% for every constituent.
